units.translation: Perhaps Zeus, sitting far above you, would hear you.
to the one newly sitting on the all-powerful seat
Thus Brunck for θώκος [seat], which is Ionic and Doric, not Attic.
where the oracle and seat of Thesprotian Zeus are
the bitter eye of the chambermaids
was the title of a play of Aeschylus (fr. 72).
I must go first to show the chambers.
and you send libations to the chambers beneath the earth
Of the waves of an approaching army
in both places θαλάσσης [of the sea] M
of the wide-pathed sea growing gray
the sea was no longer to be seen
for many evils come to mortals from the sea, and many from the land
for they swore an oath, being formerly bitterest enemies, fire and sea
there is a sea nourishing a dye worth its weight in silver from abundant purple-fish
the sacred stream of the red sea
and like a sea it brings a wave of evils
the irresistible wave of the sea
Thus I corrected for πεζούς τε καὶ θαλασσίους [foot-soldiers and marines].
near the narrow passage of the sea
and the sea-trident, shaker of the earth, a plague
struck by the waves of the sea
struck by the waves of the sea
Changed to θαλασσόπλακτον [sea-struck] and θαλασσόπλαγκτον [sea-wandering] in the copies. Σαλαμίς ἁλίπλακτος [sea-struck Salamis] in Soph. Ai. 597.

where the first hand of M, as it seems, has θαλρωτέρῳ [more flourishing], from the corrector θαλερωτέρῳ [more flourishing], where Conington conjectured θελεμωτέρῳ [more soothing]. See θελεμός [soothing].
a divinity – perhaps would come with a more flourishing breath
thus Both for τὸ θάλος [the shoot]. Which is a Doric form for τεθηλώς [having flourished], which Homer and others use, examples of which Veitch collected p. 269 third ed.
and the fruit of the golden olive, ever flourishing in its leaves
from there the life-giving blood flourishes for mortals
the stock having flourished through my marriage
if one were to speak of winter – or heat
you indicate heat coming in winter
in the midday heat it scorches the arm of those well-sunned
he compared the thunderbolts to midday heats
a thunderbolt in no way likened to the midday heats of the sun
which is said by tmesis for ὑποθάλπουσι [they warm secretly]
the heart of Zeus warms with love
again spasm and mind-striking madnesses warm me
